title: concurrent prefill/decode handshake gap causing intermittent token shifts under mixed-batch workloads
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Summary:
Customers running mixed prefills and online decode batches (small interactive decodes interleaved with background bulk prefill) have reported non-deterministic token outputs and occasional token duplication or skipping. Observed in both hosted and dedicated runs. This ticket tracks investigation of a concurrency gap between the prefill and decode paths that appears when the kernel selector performs an opportunistic kernel swap under load, combined with KV-cache evictions.
environment: Reproducible on GPU fleets with mixed-batch workloads (A100 and H100). Observed on runtime-1.18 and 1.19, failing more frequently when sequence length variance is high and batching thresholds cross the kernel-swap heuristic (batch size jitter between 4-16).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a mixed workload: background prefill jobs submitting long-context prefix requests (seq_len 1024) at low QPS and interactive decode requests (seq_len 64) at bursty QPS.
2) Enable kernel-swap heuristics (default runtime config) and set aggressive KV cache eviction policy (low-kv-watermark).
3) Run for several minutes; observe decode outputs non-deterministically differ between repeated runs with same seed.
4) Collect per-request trace logs, KV write timestamps, and kernel selection traces.
observed_behavior: Intermittent token duplication (same token emitted twice) and occasional single-token skips mid-sequence. Softmax scaling in logged logits shows tiny but cumulative drift (~1e-4 to 1e-3) correlating with times of kernel handover. Reproducible with high QPS bursts in CI stress harness ~1/500 runs.
expected_behavior: Deterministic token sequence for identical inputs and seeds; no duplication/skips. Numerical differences should be within rounding errors but not correlated with decode/prefill interleaving or kernel swap events.
initial_hypothesis: A race during kernel swap / handler handoff allows an incomplete KV-cache state (partially updated offsets or mask writes) to be read by an immediately following decode micro-batch. The kernel selection path may not be fully flushing in-flight writes to the canonical KV store before the new kernel reads, leading to misaligned KV slots and subtle softmax normalization differences. Mixed precision quantization rounding differences across kernels amplify drift.
investigation_notes:
- Added high-resolution timestamps to KV write and read ops; saw write completion timestamps that sometimes lag the decode start by up to 2ms in high contention scenarios.
- Kernel selector logs show 'handshake accepted' followed by 'handshake complete' — there are cases where read attempts start after 'accepted' but before 'complete'.
- Reproduced in local stress harness by artificially delaying the final KV commit path; duplication appears when delay ~1-3ms.
- Floating point comparison of logits before and after handoff show a consistent small bias introduced when the decode reads across the partially-rotated KV window.
- No memory corruption observed (ASAN/sanitizers clean); corruption appears to be logical ordering rather than invalid memory.
temporary_mitigation:
1) Disable opportunistic kernel swap when prefills are active (feature-flagged); 2) Increase KV commit barrier: wait for write fences in hot path (adds ~0.8ms median latency). Both mitigations reverted customer failures in prod.
Implemented canary rollout for kernel-swap-disable flag and reverted aggressive eviction policy for implicated customers.
root_cause_analysis: Root cause is twofold: 1) The kernel swap handshake protocol allowed a window where new kernel reads begin before the previous kernel's KV commit is fully durable in the canonical KV index; 2) Some kernels use slightly different fp-rounding order due to fused attention kernels vs fallback kernels, which amplifies the tiny ordering-induced differences into visible token-level changes. The combination of logical KV-slot misalignment plus kernel implementation numerical ordering causes drift beyond acceptable tolerances.
fix_proposal:
Short-term (patch): strengthen the handshake to block read entry until 'commit_ack' is observed and implement a fast atomic KV index swap (single CAS) to make handover atomic. Also add a deterministic prefetch barrier in mixed-batch paths.
Long-term: redesign KV index rotation to be versioned and allow lock-free concurrent readers via a versioned pointer (two-phase visible commit) and align kernel arithmetic paths with a consistent rounding canonicalization pass where feasible.
implementation_plan:
- PR1: handshake hardening + commit_ack gating (owner: Liam) — estimate 3 points, include unit tests in harness.
- PR2: fast-atomic-index-swap implementation using atomic<uint64_t> descriptor and minor refactor of KV meta layout (owner: Surya Patel) — estimate 5 points.
- PR3: add deterministic regression test in CI stress harness with controlled delays and assert identical outputs (owner: QA team) — estimate 2 points.
- PR4: telemetry: add 'prefill-handoff-latency' metric and alert when >1ms at p99 (owner: Observability) — estimate 2 points.

2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Added handshake instrumentation. Observed handshake accepted vs complete gap correlating with failures. Starting patch for gating read entry on commit_ack.
2026-03-07 - Surya Patel: Built atomic descriptor prototype — shows ~0.6ms extra median latency but eliminates token-drift in stress harness. Preparing a benchmark matrix for different batch shapes.
2026-03-09 - QA: Regression test added to stress harness; reproducer reduced to 1/100 runs in CI with artificial delay. Will run full fleet canary with kernel-swap disabled until patch merges.
2026-03-10 - Product (Maya Liu): Communicated mitigation to affected customers; scheduling post-mortem and retro once patch lands.
